{{Short description|Taiwanese physicist}}
'''Jian-Min Yuan''' (born 1944) is a Taiwanese physicist.

Yuan studied chemistry at [[National Taiwan University]], completing a bachelor's degree in 1966, followed by a master's degree in 1968. He then obtained a doctorate in chemical physics at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1973.<ref>{{cite news |title=JIAN-MIN YUAN, PHD |url=https://drexel.edu/coas/faculty-research/faculty-directory/yuan-jian-min/ |accessdate=30 August 2020 |publisher=Drexel University |archive-date=28 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028061650/https://drexel.edu/coas/faculty-research/faculty-directory/yuan-jian-min/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Yuan began teaching at [[Drexel University]] in 1978, as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 1984, and appointed a full professor in 1991.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jian-Min Yuan |url=http://www.physics.drexel.edu/~yuanjm/ |publisher=Drexel University |accessdate=30 August 2020}}</ref> Yuan was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1998, "[f]or the application of nonlinear dynamics and chaos theory to the understanding of atomic and molecular processes, particularly laser-induced molecular dissociation and ionization."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=Y&year=2019&unit_id=&institution= |accessdate=30 August 2020 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>
